originalTitle: US stocks today: Dow falls 500 points after Trump says Iran deal is 'over'
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a bad day, with the Dow index falling 500 points. This happened after President Trump said that the Iran deal is "over", which made people worry about more conflict happening. As a result, oil prices went up. Despite this, some technology stocks, like those related to Apple, did well because of a new deal with a company called Broadcom. Overall, the market was affected by worries about inflation and slower economic growth.

originalTitle: US SEC removes legal obstacle to UBS' crisis-resolution plan
simplifiedContent: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has made a decision that helps UBS, a big bank, with its plan for dealing with financial crises. The SEC said it won't take action against UBS if it needs to convert debt into equity (or ownership shares) in an emergency, which is part of its plan. This decision supports rules made by Swiss regulators and helps fix issues that came up when another bank, Credit Suisse, had problems. This matters because it makes UBS's plan for handling crises stronger and more effective. It's a positive step for UBS and helps the bank be better prepared for potential financial difficulties.

originalTitle: Some US Fed officials considered rate hike on Iran war fallout, June meeting minutes reveal
simplifiedContent: The US Federal Reserve (or "Fed") recently met to discuss the country's economy, including rising inflation. Some officials thought that interest rates should be increased right away to control inflation, but most believed that inflation would go down on its own. The Fed decided not to raise interest rates for now, but they did talk about possibly raising them later this year. This matters because interest rate changes can affect the overall economy and the stock market. The Fed's decisions and discussions give investors an idea of what might happen in the economy, which can help them make informed decisions about their investments.

originalTitle: Levi Strauss shares slip ahead of Q2 earnings report as investors await impact of FIFA World Cup campaign
simplifiedContent: Levi Strauss, a well-known clothing company, is about to release its financial results for the second quarter. Before the announcement, the company's stock price has gone down slightly. Investors are waiting to see how the company did financially, with predictions that it will report earning 24 cents per share and having $1.52 billion in revenue. This would mean the company's earnings and revenue grew by 9% and 8.6% compared to the same time last year. The company's recent advertising campaign related to the FIFA World Cup may have an impact on its financial results, which is why investors are paying close attention.

originalTitle: Laser Power & Infra raises  ₹222 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
simplifiedContent: Laser Power & Infra Limited, a company getting ready to sell its shares to the public, has already collected ₹222 crore from big investors. These investors agreed to buy shares at a price of ₹214 each. The company plans to sell even more shares, worth ₹742 crore in total, starting from July 9, 2026. This sale is called an Initial Public Offering (IPO) and the shares will be available on two big stock exchanges, BSE and NSE, by July 16. The company has set aside some shares for different types of investors, including regular individual investors like you.

originalTitle: SBI Funds Management files RHP for IPO; issue opens on July 14
simplifiedContent: SBI Funds Management, a company related to the State Bank of India, is planning to list its shares on the stock market through an Initial Public Offering (IPO). This means the company will sell some of its shares to the public for the first time. The State Bank of India currently owns some of these shares and will sell up to 128.33 million of them as part of the IPO. The IPO will start on July 14, 2026, and investors will be able to buy these shares during this time. By listing its shares, SBI Funds Management is giving investors a chance to own a part of the company.
